utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct. Good afternoon, Your Honours. At this time the Prosecution calls Dejan Sliskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. While we are waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, I'd like to inform the parties that there was a request by Dr. Eekhof to be allowed to produce his weekly report one day later than usual. In view of the present circumstances, the Chamber allowed Dr. Eekhof to file his report one day later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sliskovic. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you to make a solemn declaration of which the text will be handed out to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sliskovic, please be seated. You'll first be examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dejan Sliskovic. I was born on the 20th December, 1973, in Zrenjanin. My father's name is Aleksandar, and my mother's name is Milana [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sliskovic, did you provide two ICTY statements dated 14 September 2003 and 8 April 2010?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review these statements prior to testifying here today in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to your 2010 statement, did you notice and correct mistakes in the draft translation of the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of the draft translation, did you correct the word "artillery cannon" to the plural "artillery cannons"?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the remainder of the corrections consist of errors in the translation of your original English statement into the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you mark these mistakes by placing brackets around the portion that was incorrect and writing the correct word?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After correcting the B/C/S draft translation of your 2010 statement, did you initial and date every page after you reviewed it?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your 2010 statement, did you correct the nickname of an individual who you previously described as "Riki" in paragraph 16 of your 2003 statement?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would you like to provide any further clarification on this individual?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His nickname is Prega and his name is Predrag Preza [phoen]. I used to call him Prika by mistake, and then one of my instructors corrected me and he told me that his real nickname was Prega.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With these clarifications, if you were asked the same questions that you were asked during these previous statements, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 5289, which is the 14 September 2003 statement, and 65 ter 5279, which is the 8 April 2010 ICTY statement into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter. The Prosecution uploaded the corrected B/C/S translation for 65 ter 5279 into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar, the 2003 statement would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 5289 becomes Exhibit P440. And 65 ter 5279 becomes Exhibit P441, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P440 and P441 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders eight original documents that were provided by the witness in associated to the previous statement now admitted as P441. Scanned copies and translations of the original documents are uploaded into e-court. The Prosecution tenders to the Court Usher the hard copy originals of the documents which it seeks to be admitted at this time. These documents are Prosecution 65 ter 5290.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 5290 becomes Exhibit P442, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P442 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During a recent interview in March and April 2010, did you look at 25 exhibits containing per diem records for members of the JATD between June 1994 and July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were these exhibits shown to you before or after you provided statements concerning the structure and names of members of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: After I provided my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your name appear as a member of the JATD in each of these 25 exhibits?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the remaining 25 associated exhibits to Exhibit P441. These exhibits are per diem payment records for members of the JATD from the Serbian state security service between the dates of June 1994 and July 1995. All of these records were received from the Republic of Serbia pursuant to RFA 1639. They were also part of the Prosecution's first bar table motion filed on the 23rd of November 2009. The 65 ter numbers for these associated exhibits are 4975 to 4996, and 4998 to 5000. The Prosecution provided a chart of these exhibits to the Chamber and parties prior to today's proceedings with the associated exhibits highlighted in green. These 25 exhibits were authenticated by the witness on pages 18 to 26 of Exhibit P441. The Defence withdraw their opposition to the admission of these exhibits pursuant to Rule 92 ter as indicated by an agreement reached between the parties on 29 April 2010. This was read into the record by the Trial Chamber at transcript page 4629. Pursuant to paragraph 11 of the Chamber's second decision on the Republic of Serbia's motion for protective measures dated 3 November 2009, the Prosecution tenders public redacted versions and requested the admission of the unredacted versions under seal. On the chart provided to the Chamber, the applicable protective measures are noted in the far right column. The Prosecution upload the the redacted version of the exhibits in e-court under the 65 ter number followed by .1. In addition to these exhibits, the Prosecution tenders RFA 1639 dated the 11 of December 2007 and the response from the Republic of Serbia dated 8 February 2008 as a public exhibit listed under ERN 0675-4174 to 0675-4176. The Prosecution further requests the admission under seal of Confidential Annex A to the Republic of Serbia's 2 September 2009 supplemental submission on protective measures listed under ERN 0675-4177 to 0675-4251. As indicated on page 43 of Confidential Annex A to the prosecution's first bar table motion, the Prosecution requested admission of the materials contained in this annex because these documents verified the authenticity of these financial records, and the materials in the annex are of independent evidentiary value in that they confirm "names of members of the service, i.e., the state security department," as listed in documents received pursuant to RFA 1639. These records also confirm "information about the organisational structure of the security service" and the "amounts paid and period of engagement."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take them not one by one but first, the 25 records, 65 ter 4975 up to and including 5000 with the exception of 4997, no objections. You would like to have them as 25 exhibits or as one exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could please have them as separate exhibits. Based on the Chamber's protective measures decision, I believe that there will need to be exhibit numbers for the unredacted version and then also the redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think there's still a discussion ongoing as to what extent admission into evidence of redacted versions of certain documents, whether there are other ways of dealing with that. But we leave that for the time being in the hands of Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar, the numbers to be reserved for these 25 documents?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: These would be Exhibit P444 through P468, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if I may make one point, which I believe counsel is about to raise, there were recently completed translations of these with containing all of the names of the individuals on this list. There's no substantive changes; it's just the remaining individuals. Counsel has indicated that he may have concern about these additional names. The Prosecution has indicated to counsel that we discussed this with him during the first break. So if it's acceptable to the parties, if we could leave them marked for identification right now and then get back to the Chamber immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Mr. Knoops?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a clarification, is Mr. Weber referring to the 25 per diem lists or also the 40 from Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are -- the Prosecution is only addressing the 25 exhibits that are associated to the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To say so, the green ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Well, then the objection remains, Your Honour, that the translations were only provided on Friday which includes new names which were not disclosed earlier to the Defence. Therefore, we object to the admission of these lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the copies you received earlier in the originals, were the names there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Just a clarification, the names were in Cyrillic, the new translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: In the originals, and they were -- the translations were only provided on Friday from Cyrillic into English. And we have 28 exhibits which still were not disclosed before in non-Cyrillic nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There are 25 exhibits. There were translations provided for all 25. All 25 exhibits were also provided in the language of the accused a long time ago. I can go through the individual disclosure dates if you would like. The Defence has been on notice that we intend to offer all of these exhibits into evidence. The witness discussed these exhibits at length in their -- in his recent statement. We believe it's proper to admit them at this time in full. The translations that were provided recently, it took a long time to complete them based on the resources available. They contained additional translations of names that were in Cyrillic. Not -- they were not new translations provided for all of the 25 exhibits, but just for some of them. So Prosecution is willing to continue to discuss this during the break with counsel, but it is the Prosecution's position that the exhibits should be admitted at this time and were authenticated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber is asking for the 25 exhibits to be marked for identification. Any objection to that at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to the admission of the documents as a whole, so therefore we also object marked for identification. The problem is, Your Honour, that the names we are speaking about were not part of the Rule 65 ter list, and Prosecution in this way tries to indirectly put them on the Rule 65 ter list. And that's exactly the problem. So they -- these names which were not previously translated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it all about Cyrillic Roman script? Is that the whole issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, for those 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under the numbers assigned to the exhibits, they are marked for identification. The parties are invited to further discuss the translation during the first break, and the Chamber for the time being accepts that the accused can read Cyrillic and could have assisted counsel in identifying any persons appearing on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to leap up. May I just add a clarification, because I've been dealing with this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- more than Mr. Knoops. The issue really is this, that the Prosecution indicated prior to Friday that certain names would be relied upon. They indicated that by having those names translated. Those names that were translated are part of a much bigger list of names. The rest of the names were not translated; they were left in Cyrillic. We then advanced on the basis that what we were dealing with while we had to explain and investigate were the translated names. On Friday, the Prosecution suddenly serve new translations from the list of these Cyrillic names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is not Cyrillic or Roman script, but the issue is notice of what the Prosecution would address in relation to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're taking up a lot of court time with this. We're happy to discuss it further. The Prosecution does not agree with that sentiment. We intended to use the full list as indicated in the addendum that Christian Neilsen ... these lists were [indiscernible] to show the establishment -- the existence of a unit, the size of the unit, and how the size of the unit increased over time between 1993 and 1995. So it's been the Prosecution's intention to rely on the overall numbers and names in these exhibits for a substantial period of time. The translations that -- new versions of the translations were completed only recently. So we are happen to further discuss this, but if we could leave them marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the ruling was already that they would be marked for identification, and I invited the parties to sit together during the next break. That remains unchanged, although the issue at stake has become more clear to the Chamber now. Please proceed. No, not please proceed because we still have the RFA and the response to be tendered. As one exhibit, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As one a public exhibit, the others under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections against the request for assistance and the Serbian response?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P469, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P469 is admitted into evidence under seal. Mr. Weber, again, I do understand from Madam Registrar that this week the discussions will be finalised on how to deal with the confidential and the non-confidential versions of the exhibits. P469, therefore, is admitted into evidence. The last one -- no, two numbers, the second number, that's the response --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P469 under seal and P470, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P470 is admitted into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could clarify, is P469 the RFA and the response from Serbia? The Prosecution is seeking to tender that as a public exhibit. And then the annex, is that P470 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now come to the Confidential Annex A to the bar table submission. Is that the one you are -- or is there an annex to the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is seeking two exhibits numbers. The RFA and the response from the Republic of Serbia we are seeking to tender as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And have that be a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would then be, Madam Registrar, that would be P469. Mr. Weber, I asked about the RFA and the response because you had three: 25, RFA and response, and then Confidential Annex A to the bar table submission, I think you said. So we have now dealt with the second, that is, two documents, one exhibit number, P469, RFA and response of Serbia. And that now is -- Madam Registrar, could you confirm that these two documents together are P469?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So these two documents together will receive number P469.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then P470 would be Confidential Annex --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- A. And that should be admitted under seal. Madam Registrar, is this clear to you? I see you are nodding yes. P470 is admitted under seal. P469 is admitted as a public document. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraphs 6 through 12 of Exhibit P441, you describe your recruitment into the JATD. In paragraphs 7 and 8, you indicate that you had a meeting with Rade Dozet on the 24th or 25th of April, 1994. Could you please describe the conversation you had with Rade Dozet on that day?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I met with Rade Dozet in the building of the Pancevo SUP on the corner of Paje Marganovica and Milosa Trebinjca Street in his office. Two weeks before that, Dragan Zujovic, who was one of the officials of the state security, told me that if I wished to start working for the DB, I should come for an interview with Rade Dozet. Rade Dozet told me about the unit which should not be involved in the task for which I was subsequently trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What type of unit did he describe to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing specific was said about the type of unit. What I was told was that I would be trained in foreign languages and intelligence. I was never told that that unit would be involved in anti-terrorist activities and that it was under the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the reason that Rade Dozet recommended you to the unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time I was a junior champion of Vojvodina Serbia and Yugoslavia in judo and my trainer Slavko Stanisic contributed to me becoming a member of that unit. I was told that the state security service was looking for athletes with good results and that that was one of the reasons why I would become a member of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the professional background of Slavko Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Stanisic was a member of public security. He was a police officer, and he was tasked with the training of Special Police Units and special-purpose units, and he was the one who trained them in martial arts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What occurred after your meeting with Rade Dozet in April of 1994?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: After that meeting, approximately ten days later, I was invited to come for a medical examination and some psychological testings. All those took place in Kneza Milosa Street in the building of state security.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sliskovic, could you please slow down your speed of speech. The interpreters have difficulties in following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You stated in the building of state security. Do you know what state security building is located on Kneza Milosa Street in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the street of the state security of the republic, the address is number 3 Kneza Milosa, and it's behind the building of the federal SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you went to the building on Kneza Milosa Street in Belgrade, what type of interview and tests did you undergo?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: First there were general knowledge tests. The questions were like, Who was Slobodan Penezic, What's the United Nations, and other general questions. And then there were psychological tests that we had to undergo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain these psychological tests?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We would get various tasks to solve. In one of the tasks the question was related to some sort of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter didn't get the exact name, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And similar questions to which we had to provide answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please repeat the last part of your answer as to what type of tasks that the questions asked you for during your psychological tests.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were tests such as Raschig's [phoen] blurs and other tests that are usually conducted when screening candidates for such units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How was the interview conducted?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We were first interviewed by an elderly gentleman. I think that he was a doctor. And he spoke to each one of us. And he asked every one of us through who we had come here, who was our connection, and I said that I had come through Stanisic. He first thought that he was Jovica Stanisic, but then I told him that it was Slavko Stanisic and that judo was the basis. And this man talked to each one of us separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there anyone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I listened to some of your last questions, first about the building, which is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I wondered whether the Chamber would have deprived from any relevant knowledge if he would not have known that the psychological tests were the usual tests and with the -- and then finally about the interview. I'm wondering, of course it may be that you come to a point now where we really are enlightened in such a way, but until now if I would not have known about psychological tests, just that psychological tests were taken, I would not have thought that I would have missed a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who else was present when you went for these interviews and tests?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: In the room there was also Milenko. I think he was Jovica Stanisic's adjutant. He sometimes would suggest to us which answers we you should give to some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you the only person that was going through interviews and tests that day?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: No. On that day there were about 20 of us in that conference hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did anyone besides Milenko meet with you from the state security service when you went for the interview you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was Dragan Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is Dragan Krsmanovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know who he was. He was a high-ranking official of the state security service in charge of logistics, and we later met him off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were you told after the completion of these tests and the interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: After the completed tests and interviews, we were taken to Durmitorska Street for medical check-ups. After that, we were told that we should come to the same place on the 30th of May and only bring personal hygiene items.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 of Exhibit P441, you state that you reported to the JATD on 30 May 1994 at the Serbian DB headquarters in Belgrade. Could you please explain what occurred once you arrived that day?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We came to a waiting room by the entrance to that building. Milenko waited for us there, and there was also Dragan Krsmanovic. And one of our instructors, Dragan Lestaric, later on we found out that he was the commander, and we got decisions about our employment, stating that we were junior officials at the state security service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if this is the answer you expected, I found it already in the statement, isn't it. 92 ter is there to -- not to elicit repetitious evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 1 of Exhibit P442.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. It's the official document that I received then. It's called a "Ruling."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under the heading entitled "Ruling," the document states that you are "... hereby employed in the Republic of Serbia Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department, as of 1 June 1994, to the position envisaged in item 37, number 7, of the Rules on Job Specification." Did you ever see the rules on job specification of the state security department?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know the position that item 37 relates to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, but this may be the right moment. I cannot see something, and it also seems to me that this document was mistranslated into English, namely that an important part is missing. Namely, is employed for a definite time-period of one year. I cannot see that -- this bit in the English version, Your Honour. So that there is a significant and essential difference between the original and the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at both versions. Mr. Bakrac, could you indicate exactly where it says so and first point at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it says "ruling" in the heading. And then Dejan, son of Aleksandar Sliskovic from Belgrade, born on the 12th of December, 1973, in Zrenjanin. And then, in capitals: "... is hereby employed," and that's in capitals in the English as well. And right after that: "... for a limited time-period of one year at the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, State Security Department, as of 1 June 1994, to the position envisaged," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you're saying that the second part of the line in capitals, just under the identification of the person to whom this decision relates, is untranslated. I don't know whether it's true or not, but could you, please, Mr. Weber, verify whether this is the case. And if so, upload a new translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't read Cyrillic, so I do not know offhand. Would you like me to ask the witness if that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you could ask the witness to read it. Could you, Mr. Sliskovic, read the line which is starting -- I think it reads [B/C/S spoken]. That line. Could you read that entire line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. "Is employed for a limited period of one year at the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber, could you please have the translation being verified and if need be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What kind of unit did you think you were joining when you received this decision at the end of May 1994?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Then, I was still unaware of the nature of the unit, but I thought that it would be a unit that would deal with anti-terrorist activities in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: When I was admitted, there were also other members who had had contact with that unit earlier. Some of them had taken part in combat operations. So I started -- so then it dawned on me that this unit -- the purpose of this unit was different altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After you received this decision, you indicate in your 2010 statement that you and the other JATD recruits were taken to the Lipovica forest. Could you please describe the JATD facility at the Lipovica forest?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a former military facility. It was a building along the road to the village of Barajevo. There was a cafeteria on the ground floor and some sort of office. And on the upper floor there were the bedrooms and the -- a restroom, as well as bathrooms, et cetera. There was also a TV lounge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who used the offices at the JATD facility in Lipovica?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood, those were shared facilities, shared offices, mostly used by Dragan Krsmanovic. But other officers from the unit would also come. Major Filipovic, Zoran Rajic, and other officers would also come whose names I didn't know and I cannot remember them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know if any personnel files on members of the JATD were kept at the Lipovica facility?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Krsmanovic in the office that he used had a database with files about the members of the units as well as the equipment issued to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "database" are you referring to a computer or are you referring to hard copies of files in cabinets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I mean hard copies. At that time, I didn't see electronic documents much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 22 of Exhibit P441, you state that you and the other members of your training group got your red berets at the Lipovica forest camp along with your uniforms. Could you please just explain the process in which these uniforms and beret were provided to you.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we spent the first two days there without uniforms, that is, in civilian clothes. Only then did we receive blue uniforms as were used by the Special Police Units and red berets. There was a sword with four letters S and the Serbian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you go to pick up these uniforms and beret?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The facility next to the place where we were billeted, that is, in the same camp, there was also a warehouse. Apart from these uniforms, there were also NATO uniforms, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you sign any documents or receipts when you went to pick up this equipment?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for each part of the uniform issued, we had to sign a slip of paper confirming that we had received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P350 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sliskovic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are the receipts for equipment issued. But as far as I remember, I signed a receipt not only for the beret and the badge but for an entire blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The person mentioned in this receipt is someone you discuss in both of your previous statements. Did you ever see Vaso Mijovic wearing a red beret?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him when I was at Velika Kladusa. He wore a red beret there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution requests that the Court Officer provide the witness with a item of physical evidence. It's Artifact A001-3825. The Prosecution has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I see you've removed the contents of the folder that was just provided to you. Do you recognise this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my beret with the badge of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How do you recognise this as your red beret?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The lining of the beret was black. When I -- while I was removing it, I damaged the beret and the stitches -- or rather, the -- no, the screws on the badge were not the original screws. I put other screws on the badge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this red beret the same or substantially similar condition as when you last saw it in 2003?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: It's in the same condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders the red beret into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I hear of no objections, therefore the number to be assigned would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit -- red beret would be Exhibit P443, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P443 is admitted into evidence. Could I have a look at the badge on it. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your training in Lipovica, did you learn how the JATD was commonly known?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, could you please repeat your question? I didn't hear it well due to an interruption while I was listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your training in Lipovica ... During your training in Lipovica, did you learn how the JATD was commonly known?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The older unit members who had already had contact called the unit the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Between June and September 1994, did you train with the same recruits of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We were divided into two groups. Dragan Krsmanovic divided us into one infantry group and one artillery group. And the infantry group stayed together and was trained together all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What group were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The infantry group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 of Exhibit P441 you state that you received training from former members of the "Specijalna Antiteroristicka Jedinica" of the Serbian MUP or SAJ spelled S-A-J. In this paragraph you also state that Radovan Stojicic, also known as Badza, was the commander of SAJ. Was Badza a member of public security or state security of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Radovan Stojicic Badza, as far as I know, was in public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there any coordination between Badza and these former members of SAJ in the state security service of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what I heard and on what I know, both units acted jointly in some operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know when these units acted jointly?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I heard from Desimir Butkovic who was a unit member. He mentioned them being together and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness mentioned a proper name which we didn't understand. Could he please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please repeat the names that you just mentioned in your last answer.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: One name was Desimir Butkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there a second name that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I think I mentioned his nickname which is Deso.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you learn that these units acted jointly?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that while I was at the training centre in the camp in Lipovica forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And do you know when it was that these units performed joint operations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were the names of your former instructors from SAJ?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Lestaric; Drasko Suvara; Sasa Jovanovic; Slobodan Stakic; Dragan Jovanovic, also known as Bata; and I can't remember any others. Janko Keres I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many other members of the Red Berets were in your infantry group between June and September 1994?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that there were 20 of us altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you accommodated together this entire time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were at the Lipovica forest camp all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to learn how the other members of your infantry group were recruited into the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were a lot of members in that part of the unit who had had contact with the Red Berets, and they joined the unit upon recommendation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all the microphones not in use please be switched off. There is a lot of background noise in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 23 of Exhibit P441, you state that during your training in Lipovica: "I learned that the JATD had its regular composition consisting of these young candidates from the tests and interviews who received formal decisions from Stanisic, but there was another part of the unit which was completely a different story." Could you please explain what you mean by this statement?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived at the Lipovica training centre, I knew that we were divided into two groups, infantry and artillery. However, I learned from the others that there were several training camps and that the unit also had a lot of people on its reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were these reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were members of the unit who had participated in former operations and who were called if needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were the members of the Red Berets that were with Captain Dragan in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I know those men arrived in Lipovica. Dragan Pupovac; Zvezdan Jovanovic; Vaso Mijovic; Bozovic, Rajo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you learn that these individuals were part of a paramilitary unit since 1991?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The other --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the witness said "reserve forces." He mentioned the reserve forces. And now my learned friend is referring to the reserve forces as a "paramilitary group."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not the case. I believe this is clear in the witness's statement. I asked him to define the reserve forces, then I moved on to a different portion in which he describes that there were people that were part of a paramilitary unit since 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, paragraph 23 of the statement refers to reserve/paramilitary formations, so therefore there is a basis in the evidence, therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I understand that, but it is not clear in the statement what the witness meant. And now the witness said it himself that there were reserve forces. I believe that it would be leading if you immediately switched from that to a paramilitary group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the statements say reserve/paramilitary that means that it's put on an equal footing. If you think it's unclear, then you can seek further clarification in cross-examination. There was no reason at this moment to intervene. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you learn that these individuals were part of a paramilitary unit since 1991?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragoje Zvizdic, Miroslav Mirkovic, Desimir Butkovic, and other members of the unit told me a lot about that unit, and they told me that they were great fighters who had met in Captain Dragan's camp already in 1991. I met some of them personally in the Lipovica camp, for example, Dragan Pupovac. I had opportunities to sit down with him and talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 23 of Exhibit P441, you state that: "These individuals were officers in Captain Dragan's camp and commanders of the reserve/paramilitary formations of the JATD. All of them had earned Simatovic's trust since 1991." How do you know that these commanders earned the trust of Franko Simatovic in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: My colleagues who were with me described them as good fighters, brave people, people of Franko Simatovic's confidence. People whom Franko Simatovic trusted. That's what I heard from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were these colleagues?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard most from Dragoje Zvizdic; but Miroslav Mirkovic, Desimir Butkovic, Dragutin Stanovic, and others also talked about those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were the names that just mentioned all members of your infantry group?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were with me in the same group. We received our decisions together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 6 of Exhibit P440, you state that: "Sometime mid-September 1994 we started to load up our vehicles with all the necessary items for a large unit going to battle." Could you please explain these preparations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived home. I was allowed to go home for the weekend together with my instructors. I lived nearby in Pancevo. I arrived there and lorries were by the depot and they were being loaded with mines, explosives, ammunition, and weapons for a unit who was supposed to spend a longer time in the field. We didn't know any details of that exercise. We were there, and we helped load the lorries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who oversaw these preparations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Krsmanovic was in the Lipovica camp most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 27 of Exhibit P441, you state that: "We left for Petrova Gora from Lipovica training centre. There were 24 of us on a bus when we left the Lipovica forest." Who were the 23 other people with you on this bus?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the unit who were with me in the camp at the moment. The infantry part of that unit. Drasko Suvara, one of the instructor, was also on the same bus with us. The number is an approximation. I don't know exactly how many we were. I believe that we were about 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how many vehicles were in the convoy when you first departed Lipovica?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The convoy was very long. You could not see its end. However, people in the know told me that the convoy ended around Barajevo. That's how long it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, sir, is how long was the convoy when you first left Lipovica, not when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly. I can only tell you that the convoy was really long. Exceptionally long. When you are looking at a convoy in movement, the vehicles have to keep a certain distance, so the convoy obviously appears longer than it actually is. It could appear even as if it had been 5 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did your bus-stop and pick up anyone after it left the Lipovica facility?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Zika Crnogorac, a Montenegrin, entered our bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is Zika Crnogorac?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Zika Crnogorac, I saw him for the first time at that point, and my colleagues told me that he was was in the Red Berets from 1991. He was a group leader. Some of his men entered our bus together with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What occurred when Zika Crnogorac was picked up by the bus you were on?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Zika Crnogorac entered and asked us if we knew where we were headed, we said no. And then he said, Well, I can't disclose that in that case, but I can tell you that you are coming home in black body-bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After your bus stopped, did your convoy proceed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The convoy proceeded in the direction of Raca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did any other buses or vehicles join the convoy as it proceeded to Raca?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were joined by vehicles all the time. There was a bus behind us with the Serbian Volunteer Guards, and we were also joined by some artillery vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know where these artillery vehicles were from?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: They belonged to a unit which had had been billeted at the Tara camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What type of unit? Who did this unit belong to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Those combat vehicles belonged to the anti-terrorist unit of the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the convoy experience any problems as it proceeded to Raca?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were halted when one vehicle overturned. It was the communications vehicle, and that's where we had to stop. We were halted for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I'm looking at the clock. It's time for a break. Approximately would this be a suitable moment or could you find a suitable moment within the next two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We can break now if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break, and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When one of the communication vehicles experienced this problem, did you exit your bus and have an opportunity to see the other soldiers who had joined the convoy?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Members of the Serbian Volunteers Guard got off a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you know that these individuals were members of the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: They sported insignia typical of their unit. A tiger and an abbreviation, SDG, a three headed eagle, and a sword with two blades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were the uniforms worn by these members of the Serbian Volunteer Guard similar to yours or different?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: They wore overalls with NATO colours. Those were not NATO uniforms. They were very similar but not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to have a conversation with Drasko Suvara during this break?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Drasko Suvara was standing next to me, and he was also talking to Zika Crnogorac. And, yes, we all had a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Drasko Suvara tell you during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: He said that Franko Simatovic was in the vehicle leading the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the communications vehicle was repaired, how did the convoy cross into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The convoy crossed into Bosnia across the Raca border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers or other armed individuals at the border crossing when you were let through?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Russian UNPROFOR soldiers were on duty at the border crossing at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was the convoy stopped when it crossed at Raca?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: No, the convoy was not stopped. We proceeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When the convoy arrived in Petrova Gora, how much bigger was the total size of the convoy from when you had initially departed Lipovica?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: It was three or four times longer than when it first left Lipovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 of Exhibit P440, you state that it was in Petrova Gora that you first met with Rajo Bozovic. Could you please explain this first meeting?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we arrived, we were billeted in some prefabricated houses across from the monument in Petrova Gora. We entered our dormitories, and an officer came whose name I didn't know and he wanted to accommodate his men from Montenegro in the same dormitory. We objected to that. And one of the members of the unit, Milan Milosavljevic, told me, Shut up, that is Rajko Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long after your arriving in Petrova Gora did this occur?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We travelled over 24 hours to Petrova Gora and that event involving Rajo Bozovic took place some 15 or 20 minutes after we were accommodated in the dormitories.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Bozovic left the dormitory, were you and the other members of your infantry group transported anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the first one to keep guard in front of the prefabricated building for two hours. They arrived in Payero jeeps, they wore camouflage uniforms, and they transported us to Magarcevac, which was the former forward command post of the 5th Communications Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your previous answer when you say "they" who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: One Mitsubishi Payero was driven by Miroslav Kurak. And those of us who were billeted in the prefabricated buildings were transported. There were some ten of us belonging to the reserve forces of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the command post, who was present?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: That's within I saw Jovica Stanisic for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how many hours after you arrived in Petrova Gora did you see Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Not more than four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was anyone with Jovica Stanisic when you arrived at the command post?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: They were in their offices. Jovanovic, Dragan Lestaric, Franko Simatovic, the secretary Sladana, they were all there in their offices where they also slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you receive an assignment at that time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: First we were told where we would be sleeping, and after a while we were deployed at our century posts. We were tasked with guarding the facility both inside and outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you subsequently assigned to guard the facilities where Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic were located?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, we slept in the same facility in that communications centre. We guarded the entrance into the offices, and we guarded the entrance into the building itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Besides yourself, who received this assignment?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Milos Djukic, Nebojsa Stankovic, not more than three of us, but Dragan Lestaric and Zvezdan Jovanovic were Simatovic's most immediate closest guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe your responsibilities when you stood guard for Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We were under strict orders not to let any armed persons in to Simatovic's and Stanisic's offices. We stood guard in front of the building as well as in front of the office where Stanisic worked. In other words, nobody who was not announced could enter either the building or Stanisic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For how many months were you assigned to secure the office of Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I can speak for myself and I can say that I was there in that place until the beginning of the month of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would this mean that it was from sometime in the end of September 1994 to February 1995?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How often were you on guard when Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic used the office?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We had our schedules. Sometimes shifts lasted two hours, three hours, and four hours. And there were also days when the others were somewhere else on other assignments. On those days, Milos Djukic and I were the only ones who stood guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how often did you see Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic at these offices between September 1994 and February 1995?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Jovica Stanisic spent about 70 per cent of his time there in those offices. Sometimes he was also absent, probably he travelled. But I would say that they were there most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What about Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic was also there all the time, as far as I can recall. He was also absent from time to time, probably on business.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the office of Jovica Stanisic in Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The size of the office was about 20 to 25 square metres. There was a conference desk, some other pieces of furniture, and there was a topographic map hanging on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 38 of Exhibit P441, you state that "in Petrova Gora you became more familiar with the organisation of the JATD," known as the Red Berets. How did you become more familiar with the organisation of the Red Berets in Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I realised that the unit had more men than I could assume, that there were other parts of the unit who joined us, who joined the unit as its integral parts. I was particularly surprised with the size of the reserve forces led by Gaja Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The record has you saying, I might have misheard it as "Gaja" Bozovic. Could you please repeat the name of Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Rajo, R-a-j-o Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was in overall command of the JATD and what was his position?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Jovica Stanisic was in charge of the entire operation. He was the Commander-in-Chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was immediately subordinate to Jovica Stanisic and what was his position?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The JATD commander was Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were the deputy commanders of the unit who were under the immediate command of Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The deputy commander was Milan Radonjic. And there was also Dragan Krsmanovic, Zoran Rajic, and Major Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What responsibility did Dragan Krsmanovic have in the unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Krsmanovic was the logistics man. As far as I understood, all the necessary supplies such as weapons were procured through him. That was his job. Not only for our units, but also for the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say the "others," what other units?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean all the units that were under the command of Jovica Stanisic at the time, that is, the Serb Volunteers Guard and the army of -- or rather, the soldiers of Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What type of weapons were procured for your unit, these other units, and the army of Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: We had standard weapons. An automatic rifle 7.62 millimetre calibre, and we had also special weapons for anti-terrorist operations. The usual Hecklers MP5SD with the silencers. We also had Dragunov sniper rifles, Black Arrow sniper rifles. Then Israeli-made machine-guns, Israeli distance metres of the Ralph make, and other special weapons and tactics gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were these the same type of weapons secured for the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I did see the members of the Serb Volunteers Guard. They had the usual infantry weapons. As for special armaments, I'm not sure that they had the same sort of weapons that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What type of weapons were procured for the army of the Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly automatic rifles, 7.62 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Zoran Rajic; who was he?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: He had the opportunity to see Zoran Rajic often in the camp at Lipovica forest. At the beginning I used to ask, Who is that? And they told me, This is Rajic, he is the leader of the volunteers group, part of the unit that calls itself the Skorpions. I was told that he was in charge of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were the responsibilities of Fica Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Filipovic was a high-ranking officer in our unit. He trained us in Kyokushinkai and self-defence while we were still at the facility at Surcin Airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the deputy commanders have command over both the regular and reserve formations of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, the interpreter used a word that I don't understand. Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course. Did the deputy commanders that you've just described have command over both the regular formation and the reserve/paramilitary formations of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had command over all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "he," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Jovica Stanisic had responsibility for the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And with respect to Zoran Rajic, Fica Filipovic, and Dragan Krsmanovic, did they also have command over both the regular and reserve formations of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood, when Jovica Stanisic or Franko Simatovic were absent, they had had certain tasks they had to perform based on an authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who would this authorisation come from?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The authorisation to carry out any activity had to come from the chief, Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the regular formation of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: A regular unit consisted of infantry, artillery, and the part of unit that I knew at the time, that is, 40 people in all. Then we had also helicopter unit, we had Gazelle and Bell Ranger helicopters. We also had a mobile hospital which was on a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were the commanders of the regular units of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: The unit commander, the infantry section of which I was a part was Dragan Lestaric. And the others, we had -- we also had some other instructors.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were their names? Or if I may rephrase, were these the same instructors that you have named earlier?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were the commanders of the reserve units of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Rajo Bozovic, Zika Crnogorac, Dragan Pupovac, I'm not sure of their exact roles and positions and which part of the reserve force they commanded. But Rajo Bozovic had authority over the entire reserve force there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 20 exhibits from the personnel records of the state security service of Serbia for individuals mentioned by the witness from the bar table. There's a pending 54 bis application from the Republic of Serbia in relation to these documents, and the Prosecution requests that these exhibits remain under seal for the time being. The Stanisic and Simatovic Defence have indicated to the Prosecution that there are no objections to the admission of these exhibits at this time. If the Chamber would like, the Prosecution could go through them one by one for a clear record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would prefer if you would list them. Are they contained on the list the Chamber received, the table of documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, they are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are not. Then would you please prepare a list in which you set them all out and give a brief description of including date and what it exactly is. And you said how many were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's 20. We are going to be seeking 12 exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12 exhibit numbers. So we already will ask Madam Registrar to reserve 12 Exhibit numbers that would start at P471. I know that there's one number which is not yet used, that's P443, but for a series of 20 that seems not to be a good start to begin.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's already used for the red beret, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh yes, we have used that now for the red beret. So, therefore, that would be, Madam Registrar, P471 ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P471 through P482.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber, if you -- Yes, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to personnel file 3 of Mr. Bozovic already written submission pending before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would then -- a written submission. Of course, I'm a bit lost; number 3, I have no list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's a chart that's prepared. It's just a matter of printing it out. I believe counsel is referring to 65 ter 4332. This is not actually a document that there's -- it's referenced in a written submission, I believe, on Exhibit P179, marked for identification. If counsel could correct me if that's the incorrect understanding. But I believe the submissions actually as P179. And the Prosecution argue that this document corroborates the authenticity of Exhibit P179.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And apparently that has been marked for identification. I suggest that you print out that chart. Is it correct in itself that there are no objections against admission of the 20 documents which would appear under 12 exhibit numbers? I hear of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Except for number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you said, Mr. Knoops, is there was a -- there was a submission pending. Mr. Weber contradicts that and says that there was a reference -- let me just see. The third one of your list, would that be covered by the third exhibit number to be assigned, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would. If there's an objection, if counsel could state --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One -- yes, one second, please. So that would be -- on your list would be 473. Would that be -- because then we would deal with P179 and what will be P473 together, because apparently there is some authenticity issue with P179. We've received the submissions by the Defence filed the 1st of April of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution was under the understanding that this would not be objected to. But since it is being objected to on the same basis, if the Prosecution could have leave to lead some evidence right now on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on your list -- before we -- I'd like to see your chart before deciding on admission. Numbers P471 up to P482 have been reserved for items on this chart, and I do understand that only for P473 there would be a objection related to P179. Yes. Please proceed. If you want to elicit evidence relevant for the authenticity, please present it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did members of the Red Berets use short signatures?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had nicknames that they used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what short signatures were used for by members of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: They mostly used the names of different animals such as bobcat, wolf, buzzard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking about code-names, but I was wondering actually when members of the Red Berets signed documents, did they use their full signature always or did they use shorter signatures?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes they would sign a document with their full name, and sometimes they would use short signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And what would be the reason that the short signatures were used?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that on Petrova Gora once I received a per diem and Milenko was up there too and they said, Sign with a short signature. That's what they demanded probably to make it impossible to establish later who signed which document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see the short signature of Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was in the office where Sladana was in the state security building. Jovica left the office, came up to a desk, and signed something fast. He used a fountain pen to sign that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately on how many occasions have you seen the shorter signature of Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw the full signature, well, at least 40 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How about Jovica Stanisic's shorter signature?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Three to four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 4332, which I believe is marked for identification now as Exhibit P473.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move the original a bit further up so that we could see the signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This particular document is about the vetting of some members of the unit. Those are who are mentioned here. That was usual practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have in the B/C/S version the heading at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this heading as an authentic heading?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The heading was actually stamped on this document by the Serbian state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this similar to the heading that you have seen on other documents that were official from the state security department?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are the numbers on this heading consistent with the numerical sequencing of documents in the state security department?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to the leading nature of the questions because this is clearly not in the statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course the most appropriate way of putting this question would be, Is it similar or not similar to ... but that goes to a level of detail. It's understood that this is what you would like to ask from the witness. Witness, could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it looks like it. I've seen such stamps that were in the place of a heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the bottom of the document in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to where the signature is at and understanding that you are not a handwriting expert, does this look similar to the short signature of anyone?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: It looks like the initials of Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P79 [sic] marked for identification. I believe I misspoke --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Everything is all right. Everything is all right. Just keep on working. Say, what do you need?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the video that is before you is paused at the 8 second marker. Do you recognise the individual that is depicted on the screen right now?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: He looks like Boca Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could move back just one second. If we could go further. Right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that a better view of the individual on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is Medic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Medic was the Skorpion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you said earlier that he looks like Boca Medic. Is Boca his first name or nickname?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Boca was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Boca subordinate to anyone?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in combat activities. He was one of the commanders, and he was subordinated to our command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say your "command staff," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Jovica Stanisic actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've also mentioned that Zoran Rajic was a commander of the Skorpions. What was the level of subordination between Zoran Rajic and Slobodan Medic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is also leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase the question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the command structure between Zoran Rajic and Medic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Zoran Rajic was in charge of that unit. That was my understanding. But I never saw Zoran Rajic personally issuing any orders to that unit. I personally didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please continue to the 12 second marker and pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Pause right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, there's a second individual who now appears on the left of Medic in the video. Do you recognise who this person is?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Miodrag [as interpreted] Ulemek, also known as Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please re-state the first name of Ulemek?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
utterances.text: Milorad Ulemek.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is Milorad Ulemek?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC
